subject.title: [Feature]: sessions_kill should terminate all child exec processes spawned by a session

question: What public session exec-control contract and authorization boundary should OpenClaw expose for listing and terminating child exec processes spawned by a stored session?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear from source, but choosing the RPC/CLI shape, scope checks, and kill semantics crosses product and security boundaries that automation should not invent.

options.title: Add guarded session exec-control surface
options.body: Create new additive Gateway and CLI methods for session exec list and kill with explicit operator scope, canonical session resolution, per-run outcomes, and cross-platform process tests.

options.title: Extend Existing Session Abort/Delete
options.body: Add explicit opt-in stronger kill flags to existing session maintenance methods while preserving current defaults and documenting upgrade behavior.

options.title: Defer Public Operator Surface
options.body: Keep the existing agent-scoped process tool only and track orphan/restart cleanup in narrower lifecycle issues until a broader process-control design is ready.

recommendation.title: Add guarded session exec-control surface
recommendation.body: Create new additive Gateway and CLI methods for session exec list and kill with explicit operator scope, canonical session resolution, per-run outcomes, and cross-platform process tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest routing evidence is recent work on process supervisor behavior plus session/process-control involvement in related issue history.
